subtopics.title: The Toolkit and the First Question to Ask

questions.question: What is ALWAYS the first step when factorising any expression?
options: Check for a common factor in all terms

questions.question: An expression has four terms and no overall common factor. Which technique does the term count suggest?
What does 'factorise FULLY' require?
options: Every bracket must be checked and broken down until none can factorise further
Writing the answer as a single bracket
Expanding the answer at the end

subtopics.title: The Trinomial — Six x Squared Minus Seven x Minus Three

questions.question: For $6x^2 - 7x - 3$, the two split numbers must have product and sum:
The correct pair of split numbers for $6x^2 - 7x - 3$ is:
After grouping, your two brackets do not match. What does this signal?
options: An error in the split numbers or a sign — recheck before continuing
You should add the brackets together
The answer is the two different brackets multiplied

subtopics.title: The Sum of Cubes — x Cubed Plus Eight

questions.question: In the SOAP mnemonic for cube identities, the letters stand for:
options: Same, Opposite, Always Positive — the signs of the factorisation

questions.question: Why is $(x^2 - 2x + 4)$ left alone in the final answer?
options: It does not factorise further over the real numbers
It cancels with the first bracket

questions.question: A learner writes $x^3 + 8 = (x + 2)(x^2 - 4x + 4)$. The error is:
options: The middle term must be $a \times b = 2x$, not $4x$ — the learner squared instead of multiplying

subtopics.title: Grouping in Pairs — and the Full-Factorisation Discipline

questions.question: Grouping $2ax + 2ay - bx - by$: the second pair $(-bx - by)$ should have which factor taken out?
The full factorisation of $2ax + 2ay - bx - by$ is:
When a grouping's brackets refuse to match, the FIRST thing to check is:
options: Whether a negative common factor was wrongly taken out as positive
Whether the expression has five terms
Whether x should be replaced by y

questions.question: The fastest reliable way to check any factorisation is:
options: Expand the brackets and confirm the original expression returns
Ask whether the brackets look reasonable
Repeat the factorisation a second time
